newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary NABI subscription price set at HUF 3,280.
newsitem.headline: Hungary NABI subscription price set at HUF 3,280.

text.p: The subscription price for a global offering of shares in Hungarian bus-maker NABI Rt was set at 3,280 forints ($17.36) per share, the upper end of a price range of 2,850 to 3,280 forints, NABI said on Tuesday.
The global offering of 1,704,700 new shares will be followed by a domestic public offer of 65,300 existing shares, NABI said earlier.
The domestic public offer will take place between July 21 and 23, NABI sales director Katalin Patkos told Reuters.
The subscription price effectively valued the company at 14.7 billion forints ($77.8 million).

NABI -- which assembles buses in Alabama from Hungarian-built bodies and chassis for the U.S. market -- had net income of $1.3 million on net sales of $23.2 million on a consolidated basis for the three months of 1997.

The bus-maker, which prior to the offerings was wholly owned by the First Hungary Fund (FHF) of the Jersey Channel Islands, said earlier it expects full-year net income of $5.3 million on net sales revenue close to $120 million on a consolidated basis in 1997.
The company reported a net income of $3.1 million on net sales revenue of $77.8 million in 1996.
NABI, which competes in the U.S. market for 40-foot and 60-foot heavy duty transit buses operated by municipalities, sold 302 buses in an estimated market of 3,000 units in 1996.
The bus-maker, whose assets totalled $40.6 million at the end of 1996, expects to boost its market share in 1997 by increasing sales to over 400 units in a stable market.
